_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 4 Computing unit lecture film, Lesson 14 Computer Scientists and Service Robots. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow LESSON[lecture] in order: what a computer scientist does and the hospital and the farm; the bank, the games studio and the weather station, and the misconception that they only work at computer companies; robots that deliver; robots that move people and help patients; and a robot as a control system. Every industry, robot and rule named here is one the lesson names - nothing about how a sensor works, how fast a robot goes or what any job pays, because the lesson does not say.
title: Computer Scientists and Service Robots
subtitle: Grade 4 Computing
objectives: Describe the role of computer scientists in a range of industries.
Identify the role of robots in service industries, including for delivery services, public transport and health care.
Identify examples where a control system is used.

beats.say: A computer scientist writes the programs a whole industry runs on.
Service robots bring your parcel, drive the train and help in hospitals.
A computer scientist studies how computers solve problems.
Then they build the program that does it. Every industry has problems.
In a hospital, they build the system that holds patient records.
It keeps every record safe, and finds the right one in a second.
On a farm, their program reads soil sensors and waters the dry fields.
In a bank, they design the encryption that keeps money safe.
In a games studio, computer scientists write the game itself.
At a weather station, a model turns millions of readings into tomorrow's forecast.
You might think they only work at computer companies. They do not.
They work wherever a problem can be solved by a program. That is everywhere.
A service robot does a job for people. Most do not look like people.
Most are boxes on wheels, or arms, or trains. A program controls each one.
A delivery robot rolls along the pavement with your shopping.
It crosses at the lights, and it stops at your door.
A drone flies a parcel to an island. A warehouse robot fetches your order.
Some service robots move people. That work is public transport.
A driverless train runs the airport shuttle. It has no driver.
A self-driving shuttle bus steers slowly round a park.
In a hospital, a robot carries medicines from the store to the ward.
A surgical robot holds instruments steadier than any hand. That is health care.
Every service robot is a control system. It senses, decides and acts.
Cameras and a distance sensor see the pavement and the people.
The program decides. If a person is close, stop. If the light is green, cross.

at.close: If a person is close, stop
at.green: If the light is green, cross

beats.say: A computer scientist wrote every one of those rules.
Then the motors act. Round and round in a forever loop, until the job is done.
A computer scientist builds the programs an industry needs.
Service robots deliver parcels, move people and help in hospitals.
Every one of them senses, decides and acts. That is a control system.
Wherever you go, ask what program is working there. Someone wrote it.
